mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to increased policy tightening costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of over 100,000 in the following month is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as hiring momentum boosts corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100,000 in the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the labor signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 2% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing demand reduces corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 105 followed by a rebound above 107 within the next quarter is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as the economy transitions from contraction to expansion.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return during the identified turning point window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls by more than 0.2 percentage points over the next 3 months, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased investor confidence in economic recovery.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the UNRATE decline period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% in the following month indicate weakening demand, leading to a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% AND RSAFS decreases by ≥2% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the dual decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of at least 0.5% over the next quarter is expected to produce a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to higher inflation eroding equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by ≥0.5% per month for 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: When the interaction between INDPRO and HOUST shows a cross above the 45-degree line in the next month (INDPRO - HOUST > 0), the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting improved supply-demand balance.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO - HOUST > 0 in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the cross above 45.
